title: PredictiveTask
description: A predictive task over a relational database, as loaded by PredictiveQuerySpec.from_yaml. Defines the SQL label task, the train/val/test split timestamps, what to predict, and a reference to the database YAML that holds the table schema.

database.description: Path to the database YAML (the table schema), resolved relative to this task file's directory. Absolute paths are used as-is. One database YAML can back many task files.

entity_table.description: The table whose primary key is the prediction entity. Must be a key in the database YAML.

entity_col.description: Name of the entity-id column the query returns (the entity being predicted for).

time_col.description: Name of the anchor-time column the query returns; each row's prediction is made as of this time. Corresponds to timestamp_df's single 'timestamp' column.

target_col.description: Name of the label column the query returns.

task_type.description: Prediction type. RelArena entity tasks are binary classification or regression only.

timedelta.description: Forward label window (t, t + timedelta], as a pandas.Timedelta string, e.g. '30 days'. The literal {timedelta} in the query is replaced with this string.

num_eval_timestamps.description: How many anchor timestamps make up the evaluation grid per split.

val_timestamp.description: Inner-split (tuning) cutoff. Any string pandas.Timestamp can parse, e.g. '2020-01-01' or '2020-01-01 00:00:00'.

test_timestamp.description: Outer-split (final) cutoff. Any string pandas.Timestamp can parse; must be later than val_timestamp.

at_timestamp.description: Anchor time to predict at. Any string pandas.Timestamp can parse. Defaults to test_timestamp. Under the RelBench protocol, a later anchor does not advance the feature database beyond test_timestamp and emits a warning.

entities.description: What to predict for: 'all' (every entity) or an explicit list of entity ids. May not be null.

query.description: DuckDB SQL joining timestamp_df (one column 'timestamp') against the database tables by name, returning EXACTLY three columns aliased to time_col, entity_col and target_col. Use the literal INTERVAL '{timedelta}' for the forward window.
